item.title: OPINION: Enough with the ‘CEO’ jabs at Eagles coach Nick Sirianni
item.description: The term “CEO head coach,” which is a head coach who doesn’t call plays on either side of the ball, has often been used as a backhanded slight to marginalize coaches’ accomplishments. Exhibit A: Nick Sirianni.

item.title: Community Spotlight: West Side – Jan. 29, 2026
item.description: Hoyt Library’s winter basket raffle: Purchase tickets through Saturday, Jan. 31; winners contacted Monday, Feb. 2. Featuring baskets with seasonal surprises. Purchase tickets at the circulation desk for $1; $5 for six tickets; $10 for 15 tickets. All proceeds support the library’s programming for children. Raffle prizes are on display. America250 Parade planning meeting: 6 p.m. Tuesday, Feb. 3. Plymouth Borough Building, 62 W. Shawnee Ave., Plymouth. Sponsored by the Plymouth Historical Society

item.title: D2 WRESTLING: Patriots edge Cougars in Class 3A semis
item.description: HAZLE TWP. — As anticipated, not much separated Pittston Area and Hazleton Area in their District 2 Class 3A wrestling duals semifinal Wednesday. In fact, the scoreboard high above the mat on the side walls at Hughie McGeehan Gymnasium read 35-35 after the final bout. The No. 5-seeded Patriots, however, emerged victorious and secured a berth in Saturday’s final against Abington Heights by a Criteria D decision: seven victories to six for the top-seeded Cougars. item.description: The new videos have rekindled the national debate about the death of Pretti.

item.title: Pedestrian injured in Plymouth Borough crash
item.description: A pedestrian was struck by a vehicle and seriously injured in Plymouth Borough on Wednesday evening, according to firefighters. The unidentified man was hit in the 400 block of East Main Street shortly before 6 p.m. and was reported to be unresponsive with a severe head injury. Medics initiated CPR on the man and transported him to Geisinger Wyoming Valley Medical Center in Plains Twp. His condition was not immediately known Thursday.
